nodes.text: One moment. A fletch set wrong kills someone eight weeks from now, far from here. There. Done. Now you have my whole attention.

Ten years under Kestrel's banner, walking the High Road with a lamp and a bow. The road gave me back with a knee that predicts weather, and one rule: _never send anyone into the dark with gear you wouldn't stake your own life on._ I can't walk the miles anymore. So I fletch.
The watch on the wall. The castle guard. Kestrel's sergeants. Any honest traveler with coin and sense. When a watchman on the night wall nocks one of mine, he's holding my word that it flies true.
Straight grain. The saw yard saves me its best billets. Feathers matched from the *same wing*, or the arrow corkscrews. And patience at the finish. That's the whole craft.
Fly straight. And thank the goose.
